utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, you can proceed calling the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes. I can follow in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Ann Sutherland assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here with Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Is Mr. Cunningham still in town or has he left?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He's still in town, Your Honour, he's doing a little -- other work this morning but he's leaving early in the morning, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we proceed straight away with the witness? Yes, Ms. Sutherland. Welcome back, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, good to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're proceeding with your testimony on the basis of the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday, you don't need to repeat it today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you mentioned yesterday that members of the SDS deputies club played a very important role in the governance of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that was at LiveNote pages 38 to 40. You mentioned that Karadzic at the SDS deputies club meeting held on the 28th of February, 1992, reminded the deputies present that they had played a very important role in making policy over the last year?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You looked at Exhibit P34 but weren't able to immediately find the quote and I couldn't assist you because my copy wasn't marked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P34?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take you to page 37 of the English translation --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the third full paragraph, is that what you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely. The paragraph reads: "As for the deputies from Krajina I think that 99 per cent of them side with party policy. After all they create the policy. Please, who has created the policy so far? The deputies have. Not the main board."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were also shown a document Exhibit P2335, this was at LiveNote page 56 and it was the intercept between Radovan Karadzic and Nenad Stevandic on the 17th of August, 1992. There was a conversation mentioned about Brdjanin being taken fishing up to Jovica's and there was a discussion about the word -- the meaning of the word "fishing."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Whether it should be understood literally as a fishing trip?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were not afforded an opportunity to listen to the audio tape containing this intercept, were you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour I have the intercept cued if we can play the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would be very interested in listening to that, Ms. Sutherland, provided it doesn't take much of our time because I do not share the same opinion that Mr. Treanor has. I don't think that was a real fishing expedition.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can play it from the start and the first 30 seconds and then we can go to the next part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the audio tape of Exhibit P2355 please be played from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman? You have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, but my microphone doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now it works. Your Honour, the objection is this. Apparently -- first of all, the tape is in B/C/S, it's not in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would expect it to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Second of all, the persons who work in the booths here generally just use a transcript and read from the transcript and so I can't imagine how this is going to enlighten us any if what is proposed is that the witness sit here and listen to it and do an immediate off-the-cuff translation of what he hears, I think that doesn't enlighten us either. The way translations of things like this are done in this Tribunal, are very carefully, they are double-checked, a translator is able to do four or five or six pages per day. To make sure it's right. This is not going to assist us. This is not going to give us an appropriate translation of this document. The way to do this is to send it to CLSS and have them do an appropriate translation and then you can see what the language is but this is not appropriate and this will not enlighten the Tribunal at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, is there a transcript of -- I suppose there is, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, this is an official CLSS translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still doesn't help us, you say. Listen, you haven't heard my last word on -- is there anything wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It won't come on. It finally just did. Your Honour, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take your point but believe me, Mr. Ackerman, you haven't heard my last word on the matters of intercept and I haven't -- I must admit I only got it this morning. I haven't gone through your objection and I suppose you have a lot to say as I would have a lot to say and others would have a lot to say. However, at this point in time, having dealt with intercepts before in my life, in my career, from a legal point of view, from a judicial point of view, my approach is always unless there is something which at the very beginning, just before we embark on the exercise puts me on my guard to an extent as to be extremely suspicious of the whole affair, then I proceed to listen and I decide after, because sometimes, and most of the time, I have learned from my experience in the past, that it is only after having heard the whole lot and all the details that are necessary, that you are put in a position where you can decide on the legality and on the admissibility irrespective of the illegality or otherwise of the whole exercise of interception of communications and I know that you understand because I think part of it is included here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, what you say displays a great deal of wisdom, Your Honour, and I appreciate that. My concern is this: If there is an official CLSS translation of that document, then that translation should speak for itself and having this witness sit here this morning and listen to it and try to come up with a different translation that disagrees with CLSS makes no sense because he's doing it off the cuff and he's not even a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. native speaker of the language and they are the people who do the translations and do them properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Ackerman, but let's not jump the gun because listening to a conversation is one thing, reading the transcript is another. The way an expression is made or the way a sentence is spoken or words are spoken, we can detect whether there is irony, whether there is an understatement which you can't detect if you are just reading a transcript so let's go ahead and I can assure you that you will receive all the protection that you require if at any time I feel that these intercepts, all or any of them should be thrown overboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I enter one more objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor has now been informed, if not before now, what it is the Prosecution expects him to do and that is change his mind that it really wasn't a fishing trip. He works for the Office of the Prosecutor. So I object also on that basis because he now knows what they want him to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take that into consideration. It's not a proper objection in the sense that he is here testifying under oath and not as a puppet of the Prosecution but I do take your point. Yes. You know, I don't even think I ought to remind Mr. Treanor of his obligations because I did so at the beginning of the sitting. He is here not as a witness to keep the Prosecution case floating but as an expert witness with all the responsibilities that that entails. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could the audio tape be played from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you locate the transcript for us, Ms. Sutherland? Because --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P2355, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had it already yesterday, yeah, exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, what is the date of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 17th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can the volume be --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think we could pause there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Your question, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, does listening to the audio tape enlighten you any more on the translation of what is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: About the fishing expedition, I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We haven't gotten to that part yet, have we?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In my limited understanding it was -- perhaps we could -- perhaps we could take the tape back to the beginning?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the part you're referring to is on page 5 of the transcript. The tape was played to almost to the bottom of page 2 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think starting at the top of page 2 of the English transcript, it says, Stefandic: "But, I wanted, no, as concerns Brdjo, there are no problems there. Miroslav and I have a hold of Brdjanin. Last time we took him fishing up to Jovica's." Karadzic: "Yes." Stefandic: "And he scared him a little so that stupid thing shouldn't be done and so on and we have a hold of Brdjo you know, but Brdjanin now has problems with them, they ..." And then it goes on. I think if we can replay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it's useless, looking at me, Ms. Sutherland, because I can't help you. It's the technicians that have to locate the part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's what I was meaning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I don't understand the language, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was looking at you but the audiovisual man is behind me. Could we go back to the beginning of the tape, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps I could have a copy of the translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Treanor. This is English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I think I see the spot now, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the tape be played again, please? From the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Good morning. Good morning. Hello, Stevandic here, could I talk to Mr. Karadzic? Just a moment. Hello? Good morning. Good morning. Greetings, Nenad here. How are you? How are you? I'm fine thank you, what have you been doing? Well, I came to Banja Luka yesterday to finish part of the job and so on. Did you go visit your folks? I did go to the centre. And how are things there? They are fine. Are they? Yes they are great. Tell me, what's it like as concerns the political situation? As concerns the political situation, well, there are lots of problems. Are there? Well Andjelko and Vojo are going for it full tilt, quite recklessly. Brdjanin would like to put a stop to it, to have a bit of consultation and reasoning. Tell them not to do anything stupid on any account because then we are accused of these stupidities. Alija, and tell them this outright, remember this and tell them that Alija has no arguments against the Serbs. He can't, he told the Muslims, we don't want to reach an understanding with the Serbs. But he can't say why. So we shouldn't provide him with any arguments. Well yes. Nowhere. We'll do everything Vojo and Brdjo think but after the failure of the agreements that Alija will bring about, we will accuse Alija for this failure. But, I wanted, no, as concerns Brdjo, there are no problems there. Miroslav and I have a hold of Brdjanin. Last time we took him fishing up to Jovica's. Yes. And he scared him a little so that stupid things shouldn't be done and so on, and we have a hold of Brdjo you know, but Brdjo now has problems with them. Well, you have to sit down with them and tell them that I send my greetings and a message that if politics were like that, then every fool would be a politician, if things were straightforward. It has to zig-zag. We are the leading players of the game right now. Politically, we are the winners now. The initiative is in our hands. He has to defend himself from our initiative. On television, he looks like, you have seen what he looks like, like ... Like a lost man. A lost man. He doesn't know where to turn.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, were you listening?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was listening to English at there point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we could rewind the tape --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just slightly.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Last time we took him to Jovica's to fish --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Stop, stop. Could you rewind the tape a little bit more, just back a little bit more, and then if we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm still getting English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we don't have the translation -- if we don't have an interpretation from the booth and if you just listen to the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can the tape now be played?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Tell them not to do anything stupid an any account because then we are accused of these stupidities. Alija, and tell them this -- remember -- tell them that Alija doesn't have any arguments against the Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You haven't arrived there. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, are you on channel 6? Have you got the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have not got to that point yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I realise that but have you got the B/C/S channel? You're listening in B/C/S? You're listening to the audio tape in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Yes. We will do all that Vojo, Brdjo think but after the failure of the agreements that Alija will bring about, we will accuse Alija for the failure. But, I wanted, no, as concerns Brdjo there are no problems. Miroslav and I have a hold of Brdjanin. Last time we took him fishing up to Jovica's. Yes. And he scared him a little so that stupid things shouldn't be done and so on and we have a hold of Brdjo you know, but Brdjanin now has problems with them, they ... Well, you have to sit down with them and tell them that I send my greetings and a message that if politics were like that, then every fool would be a politician, if things were straightforward. It has to zig-zag. We are the leading players of the game right now. Politically, we are the winners. The initiative is in our hands. He has to defend himself from our initiative. On television, he looks like --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's comment, that word "fishing" could also be translated as "taking to task."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, having listened to the audio tape, does -- what -- what is your interpretation of the word "fishing"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have now managed to listen to the tape, and read the appropriate portion of the transcript at the same time, and the expression that is used is -- uses the word "fishing" up there for fishing. That's really all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But my -- why I wondered yesterday and why I wonder still today, how you came to your conclusion at the time that you could take it literally is that how can two persons have on hold or keep on hold or have a hold on someone simply because they took him fishing at Jovica's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what I think is going on here is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can assure you that I have a lot of friends with whom I have gone fishing but none of them have any hold on me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think what is going on here is that he's saying that they are -- have or are attempting to establish close personal relations and a close understanding with each other. And they took the opportunity of this weekend fishing trip, whatever it was, to strengthen those relations and have a chat about matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the next sentence, couple of sentences, Ms. Sutherland? Can you read them please? After the fishing. What was he told at Jovica's place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Stevandic says, "And he scared him a little so stupid things should not be done and so on and we have a hold of Brdjo, you know, that Brdjanin now has problems with them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that was what the fishing expedition was about. I think I've heard enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just on that transcript, there are a number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman? I think your client is unhappy with something. If you can make him happy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May we proceed, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told that there is another interpretation of the word "ribanje" [phoen] which is brainwashing, which may be what was meant here. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- if you were following what the interpreter, one of the interpreter's said at one moment, she said that the word fishing could actually mean something else, and that's sort of convincing or I forgot exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand your point here. Let's go ahead because we have -- I anticipate -- a lot of problems in the course of today's sitting so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Hopefully after Mr. Treanor completes his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, just in that intercept, there are a number of names mentioned. Zepinic. Are you familiar with -- are you familiar with that name?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vitomir Zepinic was the deputy minister of internal affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time. He was a nominee of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Simovic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would presumably be the -- one of the vice-presidents of the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who was also a nominee of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Savicic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can actually see from page 162 of the first report, and also in Exhibit P2362, that you saw yesterday, that Zepinic and Simovic are listed as members of the Bosnian Serb council of ministers. I want to move on to a different topic now. What was the relationship between the regions and the police?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you say the regions, I presume you mean the Serbian autonomous districts or regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Autonomous Region of Krajina. Officially there was no relationship between them. As I discussed yesterday, there was no regional level of government in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, intermediate between the republic and the municipalities with the exception of Sarajevo, the city of Sarajevo. However, various of the republic ministries had their own internal administrative regions such as the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Ministry of Defence. The Ministry of Internal Affairs had regional centres which were known as security services centres in various parts of the country, I think there were five, six or seven of them, in 1991. One of them was located in Banja Luka. The area covered by, for instance, at security services centre was several municipalities in that region. However, those were not the same municipalities which were members of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. When the Autonomous Region of Krajina was established, they -- the leaders of the Autonomous Region of Krajina were anxious to establish the autonomous region as a governing entity, as a level of government, and as part of that effort, they were naturally anxious to establish relations with the regional offices of republic ministries in their area. The Autonomous Region of Krajina of course was also centred in Banja Luka and one of the important offices that they wanted to establish relations with was the security services centre in Banja Luka, which was in fact headed by a nominee of the Serbian Democratic Party. So he was sympathetic to their cause.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That person being?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin. Now, when the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just -- there is an exhibit, we have an exhibit showing what you were talking about at the moment but we can move on. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, when the Bosnian Serb Assembly began to develop its own governing organs, it at a certain point in time began a write a constitution for a nascent Serbian Republic in Bosnia-Herzegovina and implementing legislation for that nascent entity. It was therefore a concern of the leaders of the -- of ARK that that constitution and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. legislation take account of the existence of the regions and firm up their position within the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware of any meetings that occurred in relation to setting up a Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a matter of discussion over several months at the end of 1991 and beginning of 1992, and on the 11th of February in 1992, there was a meeting in Banja Luka of Serbian officials in the Ministry of Internal Affairs who were nominees of the Serbian Democratic Party, including Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown a new document, and if it could be marked Exhibit P2364? This is part of disclosure 2.417.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that the meeting you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is minutes of a meeting held in Banja Luka on the 11th of February, 1992. If I could take you to the conclusions of that meeting --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can see there that a Serbian collegium is hereby established consisting of Serbian personnel at executive positions in all the lines of work within the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that they had to complete by Friday, the 14th of February, 1992, proposals for the coordination of security services centres, public security sectors, national security sectors and municipal secretariats of the interior.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Municipal secretariats of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned on internal affairs, did you know when the laws on internal affairs and when the laws on defence were passed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was on February the 28th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P2330?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would you take Their Honours to the articles which are relevant to the regions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the law on internal affairs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina passed on the 28th of February, 1992. It however did not come into effect until the end of March, 1992. At this point in time, I would draw attention in particular to Article 27, I think I need a translation for this so I can direct the Court to the proper -- reading from the official translation, Article 27 notes that a public security station shall also execute the regulations issued by the municipal assembly pertaining to law, order, traffic, safety, as well as other legal regulations issued by the municipal assembly which related to internal affairs. I would also call attention to Article 28 which relates to the issue that we discussed previously. This Article establishes the system of security service centres for the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It says that "The centre for public security services shall be established in Banja Luka for the Autonomous Region of Krajina; Trebinje for the Serbian autonomous district of Herzegovina; Doboj for the Serb autonomous district of Northern Bosnia; Sarajevo for the Serb autonomous district of Ramansko Bircinski [phoen]; Bijeljina for the Serb autonomous district of Semberija." Also at this time, of interest might be Article 31 which reads, "Upon the request of the municipal assembly, the centre of public security services and a public security station shall submit information, notifications and other data on the situation and problems within a district and region for which they have been established."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What if any steps were taken to establish regional institutions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the ARK assembly itself was very interested in that issue and sought to take a number of steps on its own initiative to establish regional institutions. The republic of -- the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on its part, by this legislation, took an important step in that direction by establishing the security service -- security services centres for each of the regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown a new document, it's an extract of the minutes of the 15th session of the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on the 4th of March, 1992 in the great hall of the Banja Luka cultural centre and if that could be marked P2365?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor could you explain the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document is another extract from the records of the 15th session of the assembly, we saw some of these extracts before. In other words this is an extract from a record which was made after the session and reflects what took place at that session. The agenda items for the session are interesting in connection with the events we just mentioned, took place on February the 28th, the passing of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, its law on internal affairs and other basic legislation. The first item in the agenda is putting the constitution and laws of the Serbian Republic of BH into effect and they consider the election appointment of the president; designated the executive council; item number 3 is the adoption of the decision to form the security services centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina; item number 4 is the adoption of a decision to form the payment, transactions and financial supervision service of the Autonomous Region of Krajina; item number 5, is the adoption of a decision to form the Krajina petrol public enterprise; number 6 is the adoption of a decision to form the Krajina public enterprise for wholesale and retail trade in goods; number 7 is the adoption of a decision to form the Autonomous Region of Krajina funds; and item number 8 is the election and appointment of the secretary of the security services centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. So we see a series of items on the agenda which relate to the establishment of institutions in various areas for the Autonomous Region of Krajina, including and very prominently the security services centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who controlled the police at that stage?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, in the date of this meeting being the 4th of March, 1922.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, there was no Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The legislation did not come into effect until the 31st of March. At that time, the ministry was -- a minister was appointed and the ministry was under his control and of course he answered to the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown another document? A new document? Part of disclosure 4.2078.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That document is dated the 31st of March, 1992. Is that what you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a telex sent out by Momcilo Mandic, who was an assistant minister of internal affairs in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to all the security services centres and all the public security stations around the republic informing them of the activation, if you will, of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs pursuant to decisions taken at a meeting held on the 27th of March, 1992, a meeting of the Assembly of the Serbian People held on 27 March, 1992, at which the constitution of the Serbian republic was ceremonially promulgated. And he informs people that in addition other laws had been passed. This is all in the first paragraph of the document. Necessary for the functioning of the Serbian republic of the republic of the Serbian people and it had passed a law on internal affairs which will be uniformly applied on the territory of the republic of the Serbian people and Bosnia-Herzegovina as of 1 April, 1992 and that the assembly had appointed Mico Stanisic until now an adviser in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina as minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown Exhibit P26?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, P2366. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, this is the 12th session, the stenographic record of the 12th session of the assembly of Serbian people? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No it isn't, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Held in Pale on the 24th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was anything stated at this assembly meeting in relation to who was going to control the police?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is an interesting -- very interesting passage in remarks by Radovan Karadzic to this meeting, which I think I believe are on --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can take to you page 22.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are on page 22 of the translation, right. These remarks take place within the context of a discussion about the proposal for the establishment of a national guard for the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the -- in view of its impending activation, the activation of the institutions of that republic, as we have just seen on the 27th of March, three days later, the constitution was in fact formally proclaimed and the Ministry of Internal Affairs was activated on the 1st of April. In the middle of the page, the discussion relates to whether the Serbian republic will have sufficient armed forces and then it heads through the proposal for the establishment of a national guard but in the middle of the page, Dr. Karadzic says, "You can be sure --" again reading from the official translation, "You can be sure that numbers the police are quite sufficient. I know that the Serbs cannot do what the HOS is doing - HOS stands for the Croatian armed forcers which was a Croatian paramilitary group - cannot do what the HOS is doing, to do things which are not based on law. We have a legal basis on the law on internal affairs and we also have the insignia and at a desired moment and this will be very soon, we can form whatever we want, there are reasons why this could happen in two or three days, such are the forecasts but I cannot tell you the reasons now. At that moment, all the Serbian municipalities both the old ones and the newly established ones, would literally assume control of the entire territory of the municipality concerned. The Zvornik municipality takes control over everything that constitutes the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik. Then at a given moment in the next three or four days, there will be a single method used and you will be able to apply it in the municipalities you represent, including both things that must be done as well as how to do them, how to separate the police force, take the resources that belong to the Serbian people and take command. The police must be under the control of the civilian authority. It must obey it. There is no discussion about that. That's the way it must be. I think we shall hear about it today in the form of instructions at the deputies club." I think that's the important part of that statement in connection with the relationship between the police and the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so after April, 1992, who was in authority?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends where you are speaking about. The institutions of the Serbian republic were activated at that time. The ministers of internal affairs and some of the other ministries were appointed. The two Serbian members of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina became acting presidents of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the assembly, the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina, created a national security council on the 27th of March, to control the institutions that had been established for the republic during the -- what had become a crisis and indeed a war within a few days. The national security council was composed of Radovan Karadzic, as president, and included other important officials such as Momcilo Krajisnik, who was the president of the Assembly of the Serbian People. The prime minister of the new republic, Mr. Djeric, as well as other officials such as Mr. Stanisic who had been appointed -- just been appointed the Minister of Internal Affairs and Colonel Subotic, who was the -- been appointed minister of defence of the republic. So that was the top leadership level of the Serbian republic during April and early May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And had any instructions been issued, did they issue any instructions or had the Bosnian Serb leadership issued any instructions in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. On the 4th of April, Radovan Karadzic issued instructions that Crisis Staffs be activated in certain areas where perhaps they hadn't been already, on the 15th of April, the national security council decided to declare an imminent threat of war, and -- which gave the president of the republic, that is the acting presidents, emergency powers, as we discussed yesterday, basically that meant that all powers that fell within the scope of the assembly could be exercised by the president during that period and on the 26th of April, the government issued instructions to the Crisis Staffs as to how they were to operate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Were these instructions -- you mentioned that Crisis Staffs were set up in municipalities where they hadn't been already set up. What instructions were these pursuant to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit -- sorry, a new document, which is part of disclosure 2.1 A. Your Honour, this is the instructions for the organisation and operation of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in emergency conditions. We do have a copy of this as an exhibit but this is a -- another version of it. This is copy number 93. Your Honour we have copy number 96 as Exhibit P25. Perhaps this document could be marked P25.1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it any different from P21 A?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No that was disclosure 2.1 A. This is Exhibit P25. It is different in that there is handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I misunderstood you. Yes, let's go ahead and it will be marked as you suggested, P25.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, these were the instructions that you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the origin instructions that relate to the establishment of Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs. They were issued on the 19th of December, 1991, by the main board of the Serbian Democratic Party and in fact refer at the very end of the document on page 9, in the original, certainly the last page of the -- well, let me look at this translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's on the ELMO to your right. Usher, if you can just pass Mr. Treanor the English?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it. I have it. On page 11 of the translation, at the end of the main part of the document, it refers to the -- also refers to the SDS Crisis Staff. I would remind the Court that the 19th of December was two days before the Assembly of the Serbian People appointed the council of ministers of the Serbian republic -- well, appointed its council of ministers and this was also at a point in time in late December, 1991, when the -- the majority in the Presidency and other organs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the non -- basically, primarily the non-Serbian members of those organs were seeking international recognition for the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina which of course was something that the Serbian Democratic Party was very opposed to. In that -- therefore, I would first of all call attention to paragraph 1 of this document, which sets out the reasons for the issuance of the document. Paragraph 1 reads, "Because there is reasonable ground for suspicion that certain forces are working persistently, thoroughly and in an organised way to take Bosnia and Herzegovina and thence also the Serbian people out of Yugoslavia by force, we hereby issue these instructions detailing the common tasks, measures and other activities to be carried out within the framework of the national community of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina for the purpose of implementing the decision adopted in a plebiscite by the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina to live in a single state, both in the present conditions or in any other conditions or circumstances that may arise in view of the development of the overall political and security situation." And it goes on to say things such as the purpose of the task, measures and other activities set forth in these instructions is to enhance the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. mobility and readiness to protect the interests of the Serbian people. The rest of the document then lays out a scheme of measures to be taken by Serbian-controlled municipalities in various stages. The document makes a distinction between what it calls Variant A municipalities and Variant B municipalities. Variant A municipalities are those municipalities which the SDS controls politically, that is in which there is a Serbian majority, and variant B municipalities are those municipalities in which the Serbs were not in the majority. The most important thing that is ordered immediately in both sets of municipalities is the establishment of a Crisis Staff. For instance, we see on page 3 of the translation, under the discussion of the Variant A municipalities and in the first level of measures that it should take, the following provision: SDS municipal boards shall establish immediately Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people in the municipality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Treanor. Ms. Sutherland, we've heard about this document I would say in abundance, in the early stages of this trial. Do we have to go through this again?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you just go to the back page?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can understand it becoming part of the submissions that the Prosecution and the Defence will eventually make but going through the document again to tell us what we already know, I mean, I think it is an unnecessary exercise which is taking up precious time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We weren't going to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor if you could just go to the back page of this copy number 93?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see that on the face of this, there is going to be copies 93, copy 93 A is going to Stojan in Gorazde; 93 B to Mico; 93 C states Banja Luka-Stojan. And so on and so forth, the 93 D, E and F.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This appears to be a list of officials in the Serbian officials in the Ministry of Internal Affairs who were to receive copies of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then just quickly at the bottom, there is also just a reference to the fact that regions have been proclaimed in the assembly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. Could you now be shown a new document? It's an intercept of the 22nd of January, 1992, between Radovan Karadzic and Mr. Cizmovic, and it's disclosure 2.540. Mr. Treanor, is the reference in this intercept to Crisis Staffs --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If that could be marked, Your Honour, P2367?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will be marked as suggested by Ms. Sutherland. However, later on when we come to the next witness and to the large number of intercepts, I will be going -- I will be making an order, issuing an order, that all these intercept transcripts will be admitted on a very provisional basis, very much along the lines that was followed by Judge May in the Milosevic case when the matter arose in September of last year, and then at some later point in time, we will have a full-blown debate on the admissibility of the totality of the intercepts or any of them, as may become applicable at the time. So they are not as such being admitted without any caveat, all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, have you found the relevant portion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would remind the Court that Mr. Cizmovic had been appointed on the 21st of December, 1991, by the Assembly of the Serbian People to be the coordinator for Serbian autonomous districts and as a minister without portfolio in the government. This conversation with Radovan Karadzic relates to his affairs in that role, primarily activities in the Bosnian Krajina region. At the bottom of page 6 of the translation, Cizmovic tells Karadzic: "We have formed a Crisis Staff tonight which is to operate in such cases when we cannot gather anybody so that they can gather first." Karadzic: "Excellent." Cizmovic: "So the thing is functioning because a purpose has to be fulfilled, and instruction has to be fulfilled." Karadzic: "Yes, I agree." The reference to the instruction is quite likely a reference to the 19 December instructions that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's your assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My assessment is that it's quite likely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did the SDS convene a meeting on the 14th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And where was the meeting held and who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was one of a series of meetings that I mentioned yesterday, periodic meetings of large numbers of SDS officials. It was held in Sarajevo. There was a meeting held on the 14th of February of those officials and then on the 15th of February, there was an official session of the Assembly of the Serbian People. Many of the out of town guests or attendees of the meeting stayed at the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo which is back where the headquarters of the offices of the Serbian Democratic Party were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown another document? This is part of disclosure 2. -- or is disclosure 2.548.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be helpful if terms of me finding these documents if instead of a disclosure number I could get a date of the document or --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was just going to say that, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Or some other kind of description. A disclosure number doesn't help me at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's the hotel receipts from the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo dated the 15th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. Treanor, what you have in front of you, is this the cover bill from the hotel -- Holiday Inn hotel and a number of receipts? First of all, do you recall how many people attended the meeting on the 14th of February?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall the number of attendees.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Attached within that document, there are a number of receipts of persons from the Autonomous Region of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This appears to be -- the cover document appears to be a covering bill, letter, if you will, sent by the hotel to the SDS, attaching the individual bills of the SDS officials that stayed at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can see that the total bill was for 158 million 166 thousand dinars.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were 69 receipts. We have only provided 31 because they were the members of the ARK region and I would ask that that be given Exhibit P2368.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that will be P2368, Madam Registrar. Am I correct in saying that in each individual statement, there is an indication that it is to be paid by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't understand the relevance of this. Is there some contention by anyone that these people didn't attend the meeting? I don't know why we are just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't ask me, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did Mr. Brdjanin attend this meeting, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently he did on the basis of the fact that there is a receipt in this bundle bearing his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The only relevance that I see is that your client was there allegedly according to these receipts together with people that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have been mentioned, other persons that have been mentioned in the course of the various testimonies that we have heard. Some of them very recent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that someone spent the night in the Holiday Inn doesn't have any -- doesn't prove they attended any meeting of any kind. I just can't see that these have any relevance at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I fully agree with you. I know of many persons who book in a hotel allegedly to attend meetings and then never show up at the meetings so I fully agree with you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, evidence will be given at a later stage about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Probably another intercept?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly because the proceedings of that meeting were intercepted as well, and there is a transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown another document, this is part of disclosure 7.283 and it's one page of a diary dated the 14th of February, 1992 and if that could be marked P2369?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very quickly, Mr. Treanor, is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just a minute, I really would like to be able to find these documents before we very quickly have Mr. Treanor talk about them. How can I find this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a spare copy which you can give to Mr. Ackerman here and now? I am having the same difficulty as he is encountering. I am surrounded by hundreds of papers here and it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is one page taken from a diary and it's dated the 14th of February, 1992. Does it have a reference there to the meeting that was held in Sarajevo on that day?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This is apparently notes that were taken at a meeting of the local executive board in -- apparently relating -- a report that was given at that meeting about what happened at the meeting in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour I object. I have no idea whose diary this is. It's not been authenticated in any way to my knowledge. It's just a piece of paper that is represented to -- by the Prosecutor to be a diary but I don't think a Prosecutor's representation as to what a document is sufficient to make it admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman is perfectly right. You have to indicate at least which diary we are referring to, whether this is a diary that we have had before us already. If necessary, we even send the witness out for a few minutes until we clear that up. But even I want to know which diary or whose diary we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session. By all means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Let's proceed. Are you satisfied, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm satisfied that it's not admissible today but could be when it's authenticated later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. And in fact it's not being admitted today obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's provisionally marked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being made use of, provisionally marked, yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'm sorry, with that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were asking Mr. Treanor to tell us what according to him that is all about. And he said that he sees it as a sort of resume of the decisions taken in the course of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is there any reference in -- on that page to what is contained in the Crisis Staff instructions of the 19th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a such a reference. The diary notes that -- makes reference to an SDS assembly in Sarajevo at 1745 hours and notes a keynote address by Dr. Karadzic and the first point noted is activate second degree, which is apparently a reference to the 19 December document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P1157? And to speed things up the next two exhibit numbers will be P157 and P50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to give it a number, this last document, extract from the document, from the diary that we saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We provisionally marked it P2369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: These are minutes of a meeting held of the Prijedor municipal SDS board on the 17th of February, 1992. Does these minutes make reference to the meeting that was held in Sarajevo on the 14th of February?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you briefly tell the Court what was -- what is stated in the minutes in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minutes indicate that Simo Miskovic who was the president of the SDS municipal board gave a briefing on the meeting held in Sarajevo. That's at the top of the page. It's under item 1 on the agenda. And then further down the page, at the bottom of the translation that I have here, it notes that the Serbs shall not participate in any way in the referendum conducted by the SDA. In view of that it is necessary to activate the second level of the position held by the SDS main board. This again appears to be a reference to the second level that's described in the 19 December document, 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document. Could the witness be shown Exhibit P157?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the excerpt of instructions dated the 26th of April, 1992. Was this what you were referring to earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And does that instruction include the instruction that in times of war, the Crisis Staff takes over all prerogatives and functions of municipal assemblies whenever they are not able to convene?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the first paragraph of what is described as an extract from the instructions on the work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people in the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can take you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I put it to you that this was not something out of the ordinary in the history of the former Yugoslavia, because the provision for Crisis Staffs in times of emergency existed before and the whole purpose was precisely in any state of emergency, such as floods, earthquakes and whatever, and war, that the Crisis Staff would assume all such prerogatives and functions. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we described yesterday some of the provisions relating to emergency situations and the exercise of emergency powers by Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. various bodies, usually the Presidency or expanded Presidency of the given level of government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you in this particular document now, do you see anything out of the ordinary, something which is quite an addition to the powers that the Crisis Staff would have had under the law as it previously was implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what is unusual here is the fact that these Crisis Staffs in this -- this document explicitly refers to Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people, which is -- are the Crisis Staffs established by the 19 December instructions from the SDS main board. That is these are bodies which were established by a political party to be composed of officials of that party and nominees of that party for various administrative functions, either nominees or actually exercising a function or their candidate for that position where that position was in fact being filled by a member of another party. What is usual, as Your Honour pointed out, is that these bodies are being given precisely the types of powers that are given to official bodies in emergency situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to for the record say that I am quite certain that this is a document that was objected to when it originally came up. I think it has -- it certainly has no signature, no stamp or anything like that and I think it's provenance is dubious but I don't remember for certain. I'm quite certain we objected to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your remark, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor could I take to you paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's dealing with the defence, security and establishment of power, is it not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 reads, "The Crisis Staff coordinates the functions of authorities in order to ensure the defence of the territories, the safety of the population and property, the establishment of government and the organisation of all other areas of life and work. In doing so the Crisis Staff provides the conditions for the municipal executive committee to exercise legal authority, run the economy and other areas of life."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Allow me, please, to make -- put one question, which I consider very important. So the bottom line of all this is, if I read it well, that in those municipalities where the SDS was already in a majority, in the municipal assembly, the Crisis Staff, which is being created now, of the Serbian people would, for all intents and purposes, assume all the prerogatives and functions of that particular municipal assembly, without, however, there being a representation, in this Crisis Staff, of the minorities? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And in the municipalities where the SDS was a minority, the Crisis Staff of the Serbian people would assume all the prerogatives and functions of the municipal assembly where it was a minority, take over all these prerogatives and functions which the municipal assembly would be unable to convene, and those who constituted the majority in the municipal assembly would have absolutely no say in the Crisis Staff? Would that also be a correct statement according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. Just before we have the break, Your Honour, just before we break, Mr. Ackerman said this document had been objected to by the Defence. In fact it was used by Mr. Trbojevic in his cross-examination of one of the Prosecution witnesses. I can -- BT79.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Ackerman, you're still carrying a ghost.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said I thought we objected to it. I'm not certain. And I said I wasn't certain. But still that doesn't mean we didn't object to it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. Irrespective of the fact that it was used by Mr. Trbojevic, I can assure you, that if the Trial Chamber is not satisfied with the authenticity of this document, it will not give it any consideration. We will have a 25-minute break, resuming at 11.00 now. I don't know if you need Mr. Treanor any more now. You have another two witnesses between today until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think I well have maximum half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But you have, I assume, sat down with Mr. Ackerman to see how you're going to share the time between you so we finish these two witnesses by tomorrow and we don't have any of them staying over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've discussed that with Ms. Korner and Mr. Koumjian. Mr. Koumjian is actually leading the witnesses. We were determining whether we would finish the three witnesses within today, Friday and Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you anyway. Thank you. 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I just begin by saying that I have discussed the remainder of Mr. Treanor's evidence with Ms. Korner and I will be a little -- I will take longer than half an hour but we will work out our witnesses to the end of the case as we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not going to interfere.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you look at this document? This is a new document, it is disclosure 3.473, it's the document dated the 4th of April, 1992, issued by Dr. Karadzic. If it can be provisionally marked P2370? Is this a public announcement issued on behalf of the National Defence Council by the council president, Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is a document that we referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And does it state there that if the Bosnia and Herzegovina Presidency I'm paraphrasing now, tries to mobilise Bosnia-Herzegovina reserve police, civilian protection or TO, then the Serbian Crisis Staffs should activate and mobilise Serbian reserve police, civilian protection, and TO?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown another document, new document disclosure 3.13 A?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is dated the 5th of May, 1992, and it's setting up the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, could it be marked P2371? We have the official gazetted version of this decision which is part of Exhibit P227. However, this is a document which is -- which is issued by whom, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I know council is in a hurry but could we not start asking questions until I've at least found the document or decided I don't have it or something. Because I cannot deal with these things the way we are doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I've found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Please proceed. Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document of the executive council of the Autonomous Region of Krajina signed by Nikola Erceg as president and it records a decision by that council on the 5th of May to establish a war staff for the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the members of that war staff are mentioned and the president and vice-presidents of the war staff are specified, Radoslav Brdjanin as president and Lieutenant Colonel Milorad Sajic as vice-president.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this document lists 15 members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in addition to those two individuals, 13 other members are named by or are given by name for a total of 15 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown - keeping that document there - can the witness be shown P168 and then P227?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, this is also a document dated the 5th of May, 1992, dealing with the setting up of the ARK Crisis Staff. However, this document differs. Can you explain to the Court the differences between the two documents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These two documents appear to me to be the same typed document. They appear to be set up in the same manner. The stamp and the signature seem to be in the same place. The type face and one is a little bit darker than the other. I don't know why that might be. It could be for any number of reasons. The typed text of the two documents is the same. However, the second document bears some handwritten notations at the bottom of the list of the 15 members of the Crisis Staff adding numbers 16 and 17. Number 16 according to the translation reads presidents of RP municipalities. Now, I believe that RP stands for Ratno Predsjednistvo that is War Presidency. So I believe that number 16 in effect reads presidents of the War Presidencies of the municipalities. And number 17 is according to the translation illegible and only a very few letters of it are legible to me at all and at this point I cannot make much sense of it either. That's the difference between the two documents, the two handwritten notations, the additions of number 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then if we can go to Exhibit P227, which is the Official Gazette of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, published on the 5th of June, 1992, and if you go to the second decision within the gazette?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And looking at the two previous documents, and this decision, we can see that next to number 16 is Djuro Bulic, and number 17 is Nedjeljko Kesic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Which is different from what is in the handwritten document, P168?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just looking through Exhibit P227, which is the Official Gazette, there are a number of decisions signed by Nikola Erceg as president of the executive council --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour the Official Gazette contains no signatures so --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, signature block of Nikola Erceg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, has Mr. Trbojevic made use of it, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll check later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: For example, there is decision number 5 within the gazette, which deals with the decree on organising enterprises from parts of the work process dated the 9th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's item number 5?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And item -- sorry, item number 19, decision on restricting the payments of certain expenses and salaries as a temporary measure in wartime conditions. And then the following decision, number 20, decision on the rate of turnover tax on goods and services and the distribution of revenue from the turnover tax on goods and services?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: These are issued in -- as the executive council issuing these decisions. As you stated yesterday, LiveNote on page 43, that in an emergency situation, the executive committee would report to the Presidency, when we were talking about the assembly, and that the president of the executive committee would be a member of the expanded presidency in those situations --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Then you talked a little bit I think this morning about the bodies being set up in an emergency situation. In relation to this, what is your understanding of the executive committee in relation to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have to say that given the pre-war regulations which I reviewed briefly yesterday and given the instructions on the establishment of the Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people, both the 19 December instructions and the 26 April extract, that the executive committee is a -- reports to the Crisis Staff as the replacement for the assembly. Indeed the 26th April instructions make reference to the fact that one of the duties of the Crisis Staff is to enable the executive committee to carry out its functions. The 19 December instructions specify that one of the members of the Crisis Staff is indeed to be the president of the executive committee, if that person happens to be a member of the SDS, if not, then their nominee for that position basically. And we see that on the -- from the 5 May, 1992 decision on establishing the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, that Nikola Erceg is in fact a member of that body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And we can also see too I think that Nenad Stevandic is a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Nenad Stevandic is a member who has been mentioned in the course of this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Stojan Zupljanin, who we've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Nedjeljko Kesic was in an exhibit I showed you yesterday in relation to Mr. Brdjanin signing on behalf of ZOBK and the personnel commission and Mr. Vukic for the SDS regional board in relation to his appointment?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you I've finished with those documents for now but leave Exhibit 227 with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, but in fact, I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think if you go to the decision that's contained within the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Yes, there are three versions of this document and the published version is where Mr. Kesic's name appears, yes, number 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first document, with only 15 names on it, if that can be marked as P2371? Then the document with the 15 typed names and the two handwritten names is P168. And then obviously we have the Official Gazette version with 17 names as P227.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you look at -- in Exhibit P227, if you can go to the decision of the 14th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the gazette?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which item number is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's item number 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour would it be more appropriate perhaps to mark one as Exhibit P168.1, the first list of 15 names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
