utterances.text: It's up to you. I remember from more than a year ago, we also had a problem with that list in that one of the persons whose name was indicated was wrongly indicated, and in fact he was substituted by another.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's been revised. That was in Exhibit P227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. Then there is -- that list is revised by substituting that person, if I remember, it was Maljankovic or something, I don't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your memory is not bad. Mujanic. What happened if we go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Give it any number you like, Ms. Sutherland, provided you don't confuse Mr. Ackerman's mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I can deal with it this way, Your Honour. We will keep them as separate numbers, P2371, lists at number 11, Dr. Rajko Kuzmanovic, and then you can see in Exhibit P227 the fourth decision in the Official Gazette on the 8th of May, Professor Dragolub Mujanic is hereby appointed a new member of the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina replacing Rajko Kuzmanovic. And when we have the Official Gazette, when we had that translated, initially, Rajko Kuzmanovic's name was in that translation and it was a wrong translation and we had that revised to show Drago Mujanic. That's where the confusion arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So Mr. Treanor looking at the 10th decision in P227, it is conclusions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff of a meeting held on the 14th of May. And conclusion number 1 states that "The security services centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina is to fully implement the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina on disarming paramilitary units or individuals in unlawful possession of weapons and ammunition."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I'd like to point out here that in these decisions, as in many other documents we see, the term Crisis Staff being used rather than war staff. In fact they seem to be used interchangeably in the documents, although I think the term Crisis Staff tends to predominate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P202?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 20th of May, 1992, and it's conclusions reached at the expanded meeting of the centre council held on the 6th of May, 1992. And this document is a telex from the Banja Luka security services centre, with the signature block chief of the centre Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take to you paragraph 23 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Probably just misspoke but the document I have is dated 21 May, 1992, not 20 May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's been handwritten in the top right-hand corner but the actual date of the document is the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does that satisfy you, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I see what you are referring to now. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, can you read paragraph 23?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, let me find it in the official translation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just want to make sure you can read, Mr. Treanor, that's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 23: "In all our activities we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the following paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With regard to disarmament when the deadline for weapons surrender expires on 11 May, 1992, you should take no action until the Crisis Staff makes the relevant decisions. It is very important that we solve this problem comprehensively, insisting on the disarmament of extremist groups."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this document is sent to chief of the National Security Service and SJB sectors, the chief, all departments at the CSB and all public security stations in the region except Jajce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so basically, does this document show the implementation of the ARK Crisis Staff decision of the 11th of -- 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it refers there to -- no --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 11th of May, decision of the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, that's just what I was about to take you to. Could you now look at Exhibit P198? Mr. Treanor, that's the document dated the 15th of May, 1992, the instructions for the organisation of a duty operations rota, in the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and municipality Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is there any reference in that document to implementation of orders issued by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first page of the instructions themselves, under number -- letter A, we read that "One of the aims of introducing the duty operations rota is to ensure the direct monitoring of the situation in the civilian sector in the AR Krajina and additional instructions for the implementation of conclusions, decisions and orders by Crisis Staffs."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking at the next exhibit, P197, that's dated the 15th of May, 1992 and it's entitled list of issues on which reports should be submitted and information provided to all concerned.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just going back to Exhibit P198, who is the author of that document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 4 of the document, there is a signature over a signature block which reads, president of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, now going to Exhibit P197, the list of issues, who is the author of that document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see at the end of that document two signature blocks and a seal, there is only one signature visible to me on the copy that I have and on the copy on the screen, which is under the signature block which reads, president of the Crisis Staff, Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What sorts of issues and how often are people supposed to report to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, paragraph 1 of the order specifies according to the official translation, "In order to ensure continual insight into the situation on the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina in a framework for adopting decisions by the Crisis Staff, the municipal organs are required to report to the district organs and they should report to the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff operative on duty, via the district reporting centre on the following issues," and the first issue specified is the implementing -- implementing orders issued by the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff, namely what is achieved, what was not achieved and why it was not achieved. It specifies reporting on this issue should be regular, at intervals specified in the order, decision or conclusion, and in special cases to the operative on duty when there are difficulties or confusion in the implementation of orders and it goes on to specify some other issues such as mobilisation, appearance of sabotage groups and the like.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with those documents. You mentioned briefly a moment ago that the war staff and Crisis Staff being used interchangeably. After the 5th of May, 1992, did Radovan Karadzic issue any decisions with respect to the Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a decision on the 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P222 and then also to have ready P267? Or 269. I'm sorry, 269.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, is that the document you're referring to? The document you have in front of you is Exhibit P222 dated the 31st of May, 1992. Is that the document you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the decision of the 31st of May, 1992. It is a decision of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That Presidency had been established on the 12th of May, 1992. And the decision is signed or that is in the gazette bears a signature block with the name of Radovan Karadzic as president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On your review of documentation, did the Crisis Staffs turn into -- sorry, were War Presidencies formed within the municipalities, to your knowledge, on reviewing the documents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me say that this document specifies that in Article 1 that War Presidencies shall be formed in municipalities of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina where the assembly and executive organs are unable to exercise their authority. Article 2 goes on to specify the composition of the War Presidencies. Interesting in this connection, in related directly to your question, is the second paragraph of Article 5 which specifies that the day War Presidencies are established, Crisis Staffs shall cease to operate in municipalities across the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, on the basis of the documents that are available to me, I have seen that this transfer -- transformation from Crisis Staffs to War Presidencies does take place but not immediately and not even necessarily very soon after this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland, and I put it to you and correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Treanor, that if you have reviewed the minutes of the various Crisis Staff in the municipalities -- in the region, you also find that some Crisis Staff decided at a certain point in time to continue operating but under -- renaming themselves as the war staff, instead of having a war staff being created and then replacing the Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff decides to continue operating under a new name, namely the war staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is quite a bit of variation in what happens in the localities for which we have documentation and I would again emphasise as I mentioned yesterday that we do not have all the relevant documentation from all the municipalities. So it's very difficult to paint a complete picture, if not impossible, and -- but on the basis of the documents we do have we do see variation in the process and we but we do see the establishment of the War Presidencies so-called in this document occurring in some localities but usually after the elapse of several weeks after the adoption of this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a -- I think what is an objection. It's that there is a tendency going on to mix apples and oranges here that I'm concerned about. This exhibit followed immediately after an exhibit dealing with the ARK Crisis Staff and that it was calling itself a Crisis Staff, and then this exhibit seemed to have been presented to you as some authority for the proposition that Karadzic ordered the renaming of Crisis Staffs but this document only deals with municipal Crisis Staffs, it says nothing about regional Crisis Staffs, in fact I don't think there is any authority for regional Crisis Staffs in any of the laws, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, point taken. One moment, Ms. Sutherland, but the question -- we have to go back to the question which Ms. Sutherland put to the witness, and the question was a very specific one: Did Mr. Karadzic at any time issue an order for the replacement of Crisis Staffs in the municipality -- in the municipalities? So I think the placing of this document as a point of reference to the witness is perfectly correct. Ms. Sutherland has obviously taken your point as well. If you want to draw a distinction between the Crisis Staff, the various Crisis Staffs in the region and the regional Crisis Staff, the ARK Crisis Staff, then obviously you're free to do so but I'm not going to tell you what to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No. It was a different topic. I asked the question did Karadzic issue any decisions with respect to Crisis Staffs, and you mentioned the 31st of May and then I took you to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware of any other decisions issued by Mr. Karadzic in relation to Crisis Staffs, War Presidencies, or the like?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is an additional decision on this matter of a similar nature issued on the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P269?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that the document you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision issued by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 10th of June, 1992, decision number 01-33/92. Again the signature block bears the name of Dr. Radovan Karadzic as president of the Presidency of the Serbian republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what is the decision concerning?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision relates to the formation of war commissions in municipalities during an imminent threat of war or a state of war. Article 1 specifies that war commissions shall be formed in war-afflicted municipalities in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or where there is a threat of war. Article 2 specifies that a war commission shall consist of a republic commissioner and four members chosen from among the most prominent citizens on Crisis Staffs, the business communities and the ruling party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware of any war commissions being set up in the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the documentation that I've reviewed, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. I now want to turn to the section 5 of your report, which was written by Mr. Aguirre. That section and the appendices deal with the municipal implementation of ARK Crisis Staff directives?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would like to show you a number of documents, though, issued by the security services centre Banja Luka, the CSB in relation to the implementation of ARK Crisis Staff decisions. And I've asked the Registrar to have those exhibits in one pile and if we can go through them very quickly. We have already looked at Exhibit P202, where Mr. Zupljanin is saying we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region. If you can look now at Exhibit P1406, followed by P240, P272, P294, P1288 and P955, and the list has already been provided, looking at P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman needs more time. He needs more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I apologise again, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Alternatively --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: They could go on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They could go on the ELMO but again, I mean, we find it difficult to catch up with the rhythm of finding the documents ourselves. So...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the English version could be placed on the ELMO for Mr. Ackerman and the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have it, it just takes me a while, I can't go quite as fast as she wants to go, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm trying to help you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, I appreciate it. If Ms. Sutherland could just wait until I let her know I've found the document before she starts questioning about it, that will solve the whole problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, looking at Exhibit P406, and this is issued by Zupljanin from the CSB to all chiefs of -- to chiefs of all public security stations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's a decision regard to the above dispatch related to the action from item 5 of the decision by the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina adopted on the 4th of May, "We hereby inform that you on the 11th of May, 1992, the war staff of the ARK in its expanded form together with the presidents of the National Defence councils of the municipal assemblies adopted a decision to move the implementation of the measures ordered in item 5 of the aforementioned decision to 2400 hours on the 15th of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Basically this is informing all the SJBs of this ARK Crisis Staff decision?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we look at Exhibit P240, it is a document dated the 12th of June, issued by again Stojan Zupljanin, CSB, to all chiefs of the public security stations and this is a telex stating "The Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina has adopted the following decision, and then sets out a decision given on -- at its meeting on the 10th of June, 1992, about only women, children and old people may voluntarily, that is of their own free will, leave the Autonomous Region of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the final -- the paragraph: "You are to bring the staff of your public security station -- you are to brief the staff of your public security station about this decision and arrange for the required cooperation with the humanitarian organisations in your area for its implementation." If we look now at Exhibit P272 --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Again sent by Zupljanin to all SJBs, "The Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina has adopted the following decision which we will give you in full" and then it lists the decision on the 22nd of June, 1992, 03-531/92, about all posts and within that decision it states "These posts may not be held by employees of Serbian nationality who have not confirmed that at the plebiscite or who in their minds are not yet ideologically --" I'm sorry, it goes on. That's again showing -- telling the SJBs about a decision --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which decision are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Exhibit P272.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the beginning, it is setting out a decision, the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it sets out the decision for all of the SJBs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then is it towards the end of that decision, before Zupljanin's signature block --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very end of the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is it stating there after the decision is set out in full and it's signed off by the President Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the signature?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: After the signature -- after the decision is set out in full, the decision of the ARK Crisis Staff, of the 22nd of June, 1992 -- can I have the English version of that document, please?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm sorry. That's the problem that I was having because the exhibit is not complete, Your Honour. That's why I was having trouble taking Mr. Treanor to the correct part, and that's why he was having trouble finding it because the entire decision is -- that the exhibit is not complete. I will move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Ms. Sutherland, before showing or referring the witness to Exhibit 240, did you refer him to Exhibit P406 or to Exhibit P1406?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because in the transcript it shows P406. We are correcting that. It should be P1406.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will move on from the exhibit that is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I apologise for that. The document is not complete. If we can look at P294? Exhibit P294?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's sent by Zupljanin and it says, "At its meeting of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on the 3rd of June a decision was made, section 3 of which stipulates as follows." And then it quotes, "Individuals leaving the Autonomous Region of Krajina may take with them a maximum of 300 DM or a corresponding amount of other currency."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again, that's informing all SJBs of a Crisis Staff decision, is it not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can move now to Exhibit P1288, this is actually sent by Simo Drljaca dated the 5th of July, 1992, from the Prijedor public security station to Banja Luka, and in paragraph 1 in the wake of the order of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and then we inform you of the following, that's just an example, is it not, where the municipal SJB is reporting back to the CSB?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to an ARK Crisis Staff decision?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although I have to point out in the copy of the original that I've been provided here, I can see at the bottom it says chief of the SJB Prijedor, but the -- most of the signature has been cut off and there is no typed name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think in fairness the last paragraph of the document should be emphasised that he says that it was -- the seizure was made in -- pursuant to a decision of the municipal Crisis Staff, not the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, in paragraph 1 t says in the wake of the order of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It says in the wake, not because of, if you look at the last paragraph it says that the authority for the seizure was municipal Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, and we will -- that is dealt with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not involve ourselves into argument, Ms. Sutherland and Mr. Ackerman. The point has been made. It goes on record. Then it's a question of debate at a later stage. So please proceed with your questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we look at P955, that is purported to be a radio announcement, it is part of the Kljuc municipality binders, and that is the same as P226, Your Honours. And this is entitled, "Information from the Banja Luka public security service centre, clarification has arrived from the Autonomous Region of Krajina government and the Banja Luka security services centre regarding the decision of the Autonomous Region of Krajina War Presidency of 3 June, 1992, that physical persons leaving the Autonomous Region of Krajina can take with them a maximum of 300 DM or other currency equivalent to this amount."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This document as you said is undated and appears to be a public announcement. In fact at the top in the original it says dispatch of the centre -- of the public security centre of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Pages 89 to 111, if -- do you have your addendum report in front of you? And do Your Honours and the Defence have the addendum report? It may make things go a little faster.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 89?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pages 89 to 111 contain the index of items of general application issued by the ARK Crisis Staff. And they are numbered 1 to 136. Then on pages 112 to 117 of the report, there is a table prepared by Mr. Aguirre which shows an overview of the implementation of the ARK Crisis Staff items of general application by municipal bodies. And then pages 118 to 120 show an index of relevant items and table of implementation in relation to disarmament, dismissals and resettlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pages 118 to ...

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are three tables.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want you to -- I want to take you to just one example within those three tables, to explain to Their Honours and to the Defence how the document is either black or -- is either shaded black in the table or shaded grey. And if we use as an example on table -- on page 119, we can see at the bottom -- and this is dealing with dismissals, the last decision, it's numbered 129, and it's the decision taken on the 22nd of June, 1992, and we can see -- if we then go back to page 109 of your report, that sets out what the decision numbered 129 of the 22nd of June is about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That is how to read the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see on page 109, that in the decision, and that is decision number 03-531/92, it states "Only personnel of Serbian ethnicity may hold executive posts, posts where the information flow is possible and posts involving the protection of socially owned property, that is all posts of importance for the functioning of economic entities." And it goes on to tell you about the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown Exhibit P254? And then have ready P255, P1294, P1879, and this list has been previously provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. While these documents are being prepared, let me ask two short questions to the witness. This part that you are being referred to, Mr. Treanor, was not prepared by you, was not co-authored by you, and was not prepared by your department but by someone outside your department, and you took the decision to incorporate it as a section in your report. My question to you is the following: Yesterday you said that you take full responsibility for what is contained in this section, and I take your word for it. What I want to know is whether you went through the conclusions and the diagrams and the graphs and whatever we have here in this particular section of the report prepared by Mr. Aguirre and whether you are in a position to swear, to confirm on oath, that his conclusions are correct, whether you have verified them and found them to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness answers I was going to provide Your Honour was an updated schedule in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which are these?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in the meantime I want to know whether the witness, before coming here, did go through the conclusions reached by Mr. Aguirre and whether he shares those same conclusions, having verified them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The section of the report written by Mr. Aguirre consists of two parts, the main text which is section 5 of the report, and then the appendices which relate to that section of the report. I closely read the text of the report, discussed it with Mr. Aguirre, suggested certain changes to clarify certain points, and correct some points to me which seem to be in need of correction. And I reviewed the tables themselves. I did not, however, go back and read every document referred to in the tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And relate them to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Thank you, Mr. Treanor. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, along that same line, Your Honour, it might be useful for future planning to inquire whether in view of what Mr. Treanor has just told you he's actually prepared to be cross-examined in detail about any of the matters contained in these tables that he didn't prepare because that's more important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's more important obviously but that's why I put the question to him yesterday whether he was prepared to assume responsibility for that chapter because if he does then obviously, he cannot decline to be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if my memory serves me correctly, Ms. Korner advised the Court and the Defence, I think you referred to the conversation yesterday morning, that if there was going to be any cross-examination, if Mr. Ackerman was going to take objection to any parts of section 5 in relation to the appendices, then it was Mr. Aguirre who was going to have to be cross-examined on that and not Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In my country, the way -- and in other countries, the way we do it is that if a report is the joint effort of several persons, that other person or persons, or those other persons, can be asked to join in the course of the testimony. They will sit to the right or the left of Mr. Treanor and if there is any part of the report that is being contested on cross-examination, then the other person can be sworn in and the cross-examination directed to him. I would definitely open all doors for you, Ms. Sutherland, for Ms. Korner and for Mr. Ackerman to make that possible. I have tried to get as much information, as much confirmation from Mr. Treanor myself because I have full trust in Mr. Treanor, but if there comes a point when we need Mr. Aguirre, Xavier Aguirre, he had obviously be prepared to bring him over because the way he has answered the question today, it is obvious that there may be some points that only Mr. Aguirre could answer. So I would have absolutely no objection of having him sitting next to him present during the testimony of Mr. Treanor and then being ready to answer any question put to him on cross-examination or even by you or Ms. Korner. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that agreeable to you, Mr. Ackerman as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in relation to the -- what we have just gone through, the pages 112 to 117 of the addendum, I have an updated list. Your Honour, Mr. Treanor and I discussed the other day showing Your Honour an example from each of the three, disarmament example a dismissal and a resettlement example to show you how the boxes were shaded either black or grey. For time constraints I'm only going to take Mr. Treanor to one but in relation to us discussing the disarmament example that I wanted to use it became apparent that if you look at the report, on page 120 -- sorry, 118, for disarmament, the decision numbered 20, issued by the ARK Crisis Staff on the 11th of May we can see Prijedor black, Sanski Most black, Kljuc black and Kotor Varos black. In fact, when we reviewed the document together it became apparent that that should have been shaded grey. And Mr. Aguirre agreed with that. There was also one in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that you are, for all intents and purposes, making a declaration that this new sheet of paper which will be given a number will for all intents and purposes replace page 118 of the report, correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move ahead and go through them one by one, all the replacements, are these also to replace the originals in the report or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, pages 112 to 117.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Will be replaced by these pages which are numbered 1 to 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. And then you have appendix 4.4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I've just said about the disarmament one the other one is dismissals when we on page 120, for the -- sorry, resettlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait a bit. Let's go through them one by one. Appendix 4.3, disarmament, this is going to -- first of all what number are you going to give this new entry? P --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: P2351.1, Your Honour because the report is P2351.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. Then I have appendix 4.4 which is dismissals. And it's taken that P2351 will replace page 118 in the addendum report, correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 4.4 replaces --

utterances.text: No, 4.3, the one we have just marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 4.3 disarmament replaces page --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 118, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now appendix 4.4, dismissals, and that replaces page 119, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it will be marked P2351.2, correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for agreeing with me, Ms. Gustin. And then there is appendix 4.2, which is overview of implementation of ARK Crisis Staff items of general application, and that starts, I have one, two, three, four, five, six sheets of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour that's where I got confused because I thought we marked this, the overview, as the -- as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that starts with page 112 through and up to 117, correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that will be marked P2351.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And now given also that Mr. Treanor and I found these two instances where the black box should have been shaded grey, we undertake to -- Mr. Aguirre undertakes to recheck every box and if there are any further discrepancies we will provide them to the Defence and Your Honours immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, if we can take, using dismissals as an example, and that was --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, when you looked at this document, it was determined that it was not conclusive evidence and therefore that was why it was determined to change this box from black to grey, was it not?

utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to disarmament, and that was another one that had been amended, I just want to quickly take you to the Kotor Varos document, where it was shaded black and it's now been determined that it should be shaded grey.

utterances.text: If the witness could be shown, please, P631? utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I've just noticed something just in relation to this last thing that we were talking about. So I will need to go back to that quickly. So if I can move on, Your Honour -- Your Honours, I'm sorry -- to -- if you turn to page 90 of the report -- not page 90, I'm sorry. Yes, 90. That sets out, if we look at decision number 9, that's an ARK Crisis Staff decision of the 8th of May, 1992, and in the conclusion, it's for the presidents of the national defence councils to supplied detailed information to the war staff of the ARK about mobilisation in their municipalities and if we go now to page 112, which is the overview of the implementation of the items, and we look at decision number 9, we can see for Bosanski Petrovac it is blank but if we look at the new table that was given to Your Honours a moment ago, P2351.3, and we look at decision number 9, we can see that it's now black and I want to now go to that document which is a new document which was provided by Mr. Hidic, if you recall, after he testified he said that he had a number of documents, and this is one of the documents and it was disclosed to the Defence on the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So Mr. Treanor, you can close your report now. We have finished with the implementation of the ARK Crisis Staff decisions. Are you aware of Mr. Brdjanin's appointments after September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain to the Court what position he took up?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, it was necessary to observe that in September, 1992, the Bosnian Serb assembly abolished the regional structure within the republic. That is it abolished the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the other Serbian autonomous districts. At the same time -- virtually the same time, on September the 15th, the assembly appointed Radoslav Brdjanin to be an acting vice-president of the government of the Republika Srpska, and at the same time, also appointed Nikola Erceg, who was the -- until that time had been the president of the executive council of ARK, to be a minister in the government. That government continued in office until the -- technically until in January 1993. In November, 1992, Mr. Djeric, Branko Djeric, the president of the government resigned which entailed the formation of a new government which was formed at the beginning of January -- 23 January, 1993. Vladimir Lukic was the new president of that government, that is prime minister and Mr. Brdjanin was named to be a minister in that government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically as I take it he was acting or deputy prime minister from September to the 23rd of January at the latest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: After that, he became a minister? In the new government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to the deputy prime ministers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How many of them there were?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I have an Official Gazette here. I don't have an English translation of it but if I could provide this to Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the decision of the 20th of January, in fact, 1993, passed by the assembly electing the new government.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who does it name there as vice-president?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Ostojic is named as vice-president of the government for the economy and Vitomir Popovic as vice-president of the government for internal policy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does that satisfy Your Honours' questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware whether they held the posts throughout 1993?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK JOSEPH TREANOR [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Treanor, as I explained to you earlier on, cross-examination will take place sometime in October, I would say, and so your testimony for the time being -- I should like to take this opportunity to thank you for bearing with us. I know it's not an easy topic to deal with, and your report is -- covers a lot of territory and must be tiring also for you to testify on it. So I do appreciate your cooperation and your patience and your testimony has been extremely helpful for this Tribunal. We will certainly see you again and until then, we wish you some holidays at least. Some holidays. Yes Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just publicly like to thank Mr. Treanor for bearing with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not easy. I mean I realize that this was one of the heaviest testimonies we had and it just -- there is no way you can avoid it because it's technical and complicated in itself. utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: There is an application I would make in relation to Mr. Treanor and also in order to Mr. Brown and that is that the Office of the Prosecutor be allowed to converse with Mr. Treanor, certainly not on any matters relating to his evidence, and the same for Mr. Brown, but because of the functions, the position that Mr. Treanor holds and also Mr. Brown in the military analyst's unit we need to be able to talk to them on other matters and if it wasn't for Mr. Ackerman's request to postpone cross-examination, then it normally wouldn't have caused a problem but if it's not going to happen for the next three months it's going to create difficulties in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I intervened when we had the case of the expert on propaganda. Any way, but the answer basically is yes. utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You understood what's going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usually until your testimony is complete, you should not allow anyone to approach you or discuss anything with you, but things being what they are, in other words that the cross-examination will take place in a few months' time, and knowing that the Prosecution may need to discuss other matters with you, they are being granted permission to approach you and provided you are approached on other matters and not the contents of your testimony, then obviously you are free and you have every right to cooperate with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you once more, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I think I see Mr. Koumjian, you are taking over. I think we ought to remain in open session until we clear up the preliminaries and then we go into closed session if we decide to start hearing the witness. Do you agree, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was just wondering if it would cause horrible difficulties if we adjourn for the day? Since there is only 30 minutes left anyhow. Otherwise I'm going to have to ask for about a ten minute recess anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would prefer the ten minute recess. I understand Mr. Ackerman's problem, hoping that at least one witness will finish this week, if not both, so that we can send at least one person home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest -- I will give the break because I'm not going to question that. On the other hand, I think if you follow the procedure that we have adopted these last few weeks, in other words meet beforehand, you and the Defence, and agree before how you're going to split the time that you have to finish these next three witnesses, it would be extremely more helpful. In the meantime, this morning, I think after this short break that we are conceding, we need to discuss some preliminaries, particularly in view of the motion filed by Mr. Ackerman and handed to us this morning, which I have -- which we have gone through and which requires at least some preliminary comments and measures to be taken before we start with the next witness. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Fine. Just remind you the next witness is in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that but the preliminaries need not be, provided we don't mention names, I think the preliminaries ought to be in public, in open session, and it's very important that they are in open session. I don't want to have anything in secret dealing with these matters. Thank you. --- Break taken at 1.19 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, where is Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, he just raced upstairs to get the case law in case Mr. Ackerman was going to argue it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We are not going to argue any case law today. Certainly not going to argue case law not having given you the time to file a response to Mr. Ackerman's motion. Of course, if you want to take the next 15 minutes to respond to it orally, you can do that and we can come with an oral decision tomorrow morning but basically, I can anticipate what our oral decision is going to be, that, as I explained earlier on, this is a serious matter which deserves the utmost attention. The admissibility of intercept telephone conversations involves basically two legal -- basic legal aspects. One is that of legality, whether they have been legally obtained, and second is the question of authenticity. The first one is complicated and requires some debate. The second one, I dare say, without the least reservation, that I -- together with my two colleagues, would be in a position to reach a conclusion only after having heard evidence and having gone through what happened in other cases and having also read the statements that have been given, not all of them, because most of them came this morning, but what I had yesterday, that's five statements I went through, we will need to wait until we are in a position to decide on this matter, and I think it would be most unfair on us and on you in particular, to force it on you to debate the legal issues involved before we have concluded all the evidence on these transcripts, on these -- on the transcripts of these intercepts and heard all the evidence. I think that is of the utmost importance. The position that we are taking therefore basically for the time being is that we will admit all the intercepts that the Prosecution proposes to tender into evidence for the time being, with the big caveat that we'll just give them a number, allow witnesses to make reference to them, and then with the understanding that at the end of the story, we will then decide whether they will continue to form part of the records of this case or whether they will be just expunged, taken out of the records and forgotten. It wouldn't have been a wasted time if we come to that conclusion because the matter is of the utmost importance. If they are legal and authentic, then they obviously deserve a place. If they are not legal or if they are not authentic, or if they are neither of the two, neither legal nor authentic, then obviously we still have to decide whether under Rule 95 we should admit them because Rule 95 leaves no such discretion to this Tribunal. It is a mandatory clause, if they are -- do not satisfy the test established under Rule 95, our obligation is to throw them overboard. So that's the position. Any comments, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a couple of things. The motion was produced hastily. I actually was -- started working on it at 4.30 this morning so I noticed that in that section of the motion where I discuss the case -- the Delalic case and the statement of Mr. Music that was dealt with pursuant to Rule 95, I'm not sure I made it clear that the issue there was slightly different in that the statement was taken by the Austrian police in accordance with Austrian law. So -- as far as Austrian law was concerned, there was no violation but the issue there was that it violated at least the law of this Tribunal as well as some international covenants and that sort of thing. That's a difference I'm not sure I pointed out as clearly as I should have. The other thing is that you asked me yesterday about -- when you made an oral ruling on a motion about two witnesses, 7.189 and 7.278, about whether I would want them brought for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have looked at their statements, Your Honour, and I think primarily they go to the technical aspects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Of these, and so that's not a very -- I don't think there would be any need to cross-examine them regarding the technical aspects of these intercepts. There is a witness, 7.241, however, who was significant information regarding the legality of these matters who probably should be brought for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Koumjian, and one other thing before you -- Mr. Ackerman, I also notice in paragraph 13 of your motion that you have stated that Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic were the SDA members of the Presidency so I think you owe both of them an apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do. And that was probably at 5.15 this morning that that mistake was made and thank you for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will respond in writing today to the first issue that Your Honour raised, the issue raised in Mr. Ackerman's motion, the legality of the admission of these intercepts under Rule 95. The witnesses will address the second issue that Your Honour raised which is the authenticity. I understand Mr. Ackerman gave a hasty, the time pressures on him to produce his motion. Also we are under time pressure to produce a response but I would like if Your Honours would give me a moment to add a few comments orally regarding that. We do take the position that the domestic laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina were complied with, but it's my submission to Your Honours that this Tribunal should not be determining on a case-by-case basis whether or not evidence admitted here complies with the domestic law. It would lead to what I think could be the rather absurd position, for example, that one piece of evidence is admissible under Bosnian law, not admissible under Croatian law, admissible under the laws of Macedonia, not admissible under the laws of Yugoslavia. In addition when we are dealing with evidence that's going to war crimes and crimes against humanity, Your Honours know that often the very best evidence comes from electronic eavesdropping, not only by parties to the dispute, political or in armed conflict but by third parties and the -- this is going to be very probative evidence that is done by all -- virtually all countries around the world. I think it would have a very bad effect on future Prosecutions of these very serious crimes if the Court takes the position that it's going to exclude evidence that's electronically obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I never said that, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm just raising the issue for something for Your Honours to consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With regard to legality if you follow the proceedings or the transcript of the proceedings in the case against Slobodan Milosevic, going back to the 27th and 30th of September of last year, you will immediately see that the Trial Chamber then did attach great importance to the question of legality as being always and constantly in the background of any decision it might have to take later on and in that case, it never came to a decision, and I don't know if in this case we would need to come to a decision but the question of legality obviously plays an important part, as the question of authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My position is, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One of the witnesses you're bringing forward saying I'm not in a position to testify -- I'm not in a position to recognise, for example, Mr. Brdjanin's voice. So where do you take it up from there you will have to find a solution if you are faced with that problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, going back to the legality issue Your Honour. Another point I wanted to bring to Your Honour's attention, is that all of the intercepts that we are offering were recorded before the creation of this Tribunal. The exclusionary rule that exists in -- where it does exist and many countries do not have it, it exists for the purposes of a prophylactic rule to prevent abuses by the police. In this case, this Tribunal did not even exist at the time of these interceptions took place. And, in fact, Your Honours know that whatever this Court rules or this Tribunal rules electronic interceptions are going to take place around the world. You're not going to stop it by not admitting it in war crimes trials. The only result will be that very important evidence would be excluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would even recommend it as absolutely necessary. And I come incidentally so that you -- both of you are aware of this, I come from a jurisdiction where the exclusionary rule is not adopted, is not applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are -- my country, we are a far cry from what the position is in the States and I would say very, very near to what the position is in the United Kingdom. That's the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If Your Honour could indulge me for a couple of more minutes we get such a few opportunities to talk about the law and domestic law. One thing I would point out as Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham would know from United States practice is that, in fact, if this was a case in the United States, the only intercepts which Mr. Brdjanin would have standing to challenge would be those in which he himself is a party. The Defence here has challenged all intercepts, the majority of those Mr. Brdjanin is not even a party to. And I think it would lead to a very absurd result if we looked at national laws in one country, a third country is intercepting conversations and that would be admissible because under their national security it's admissible while another country in this case, very involved in the situation, Bosnia-Herzegovina, their interceptions would not be admissible. They are the ones most affected because it violates, reportedly violates the national law. Again it's our position which we will give in the written motion that this, in fact, was in compliance with the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the position therefore is as follows. The legal debate will take place at the appropriate time. It also means that we will be expecting a written response from you and if you want to update your objection at a later point after having had more time to think about it, Mr. Ackerman, you are free to do so. In other words, to replace your objection with a more comprehensive document. You are free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate it very much because I think it would enhance its credibility if I could do that and I would be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On my part I will be studying the motions and response that were filed in Krajisnik Plavsic. I haven't gone through those as yet. I don't know the relevance but I still have to go into those. And other -- and other documents of this Tribunal. The intercepts are being admitted with the caveat that I explained earlier on, and Mr. Koumjian, you're free to make use of any one of them with any of the witnesses you intend to bring forward, then we decide at a later stage on what will require a decision. All right? Shall we bring in the witness? And I explain to him --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I just want to make sure that nobody believes that I'm challenging the admissibility of electronic surveillance evidence per se. I'm not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a question, I have had to deal with it in my country just as I have had to deal with exclusionary evidence, eavesdropping even by third parties not involved in the police or in the security services so it's not a new subject. It's not a subject that I like but it's not a new subject. Neither this nor the exclusionary rule. All right? Do you want to bring in the witness or do you want to explain to him yourself, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to show his face now or do you want to show his face tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Koumjian, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Explain to him that we do apologise to him for having kept him here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Koumjian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let me please put the Defence and Your Honours -- I wanted to authenticate these documents, it may not be apparent from the statements. A witness that's going to testify has provided many of these to us and many others -- a few others have come from other persons associated with the same organisation. We are preparing a declaration by an investigator indicating the source of each of the individual intercepts that we got, in other words who it was that provided it on such and such a date and that will be provided as a 92 bis declaration submitted to the Court, just to link the individual intercepts with how we obtained it. I will not ask the witness to go through each intercept. I think it would be a waste of the Court's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will need to explain, for example, going through one of the statements yesterday I came across specific reference to one intercept which was made use of either yesterday or the day before by Mr. Treanor and that's the intercept of the telephone conversation dated 17th and 18th of December, I think -- or of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: August, Ms. Sutherland says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It seems to me that this witness refers to it and says that the date is wrong. It was March or May. So prepare yourselves because when it comes to authenticity, you will have to prove well beyond reasonable doubt. If we have a doubt about a single -- the authenticity of a single intercept, we'll throw it out straight away. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We will discuss it. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. See you tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
